top_signals.title: Oil Prices Head for 12% Weekly Loss Despite Fresh Tanker Attacks
top_signals.summary: Crude oil prices were on course for a sharp weekly drop, with both Brent crude and WTI shedding 12% since Monday, following the results of the U.S. midterm elections, which gave rise to hopes that the war in the Middle East could be brought to a swift end. At the time of writing, Brent crude was trading at $99.42 per barrel, and West Texas Intermediate was trading at $91.242 per barrel, both up from Thursday’s close on reports of fresh tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz. Reuters reported at least five vessel incidents in the Persian Gulf…

top_signals.title: U.S. Shale Giants Hold Back on Drilling Despite Higher Oil Prices
top_signals.summary: The biggest U.S. shale producers have remained conservative in spending on drilling this year despite the spike in the average WTI crude price by $20 per barrel compared to last year. While signs have emerged that smaller independents have started to take advantage of the higher oil prices to increase drilling, the biggest shale producers are keeping their powder dry amid unprecedented uncertainty in global markets.
